sell.heroTagline: Put a tablet on the counter and turn it into a self-ordering station — customers tap to order, the shop manages one live queue.
sell.heroBadge: Sales playbook · for the sales team

prepare.title: Prepare before the field visit
prepare.subtitle: Checklist before you walk into the shop
prepare.item1: Tablet/phone fully charged, kiosk mode or demo ready to open
prepare.item2: Have /info open to showcase features and /tutorial for a step-by-step demo
prepare.item3: Demo links ready: home page with the shop map · /info · /tutorial — bookmark them on the device
prepare.item4: Know the pricing model: prepaid daily service via PromptPay, per the shop's plan — details on /info; never quote a made-up number
prepare.item5: Log in as admin with /admin/leads open, ready to register the shop on-site
prepare.item6: Bring a business card / LINE QR so the owner can follow up on the spot

open.title: Opening script (30 seconds)
open.subtitle: Start with the shop's daily problem, not with the product
open.script1: "How long do your queues get on a rush? Some shops we visit have lines reaching the street — customers give up and staff stretch themselves taking orders, billing, and serving."
open.script2: "There's a simple way: a tablet on the counter. Customers tap to order themselves, prices are exact, and the shop sees every order in one live queue. May I show you in 2–3 minutes?"

pains.title: Pain → how Easy Order fixes it
pains.subtitle: Listen for which pain the shop has, then speak to that one
pains.pain1: Long counter queues, too few staff
pains.fix1: Customers tap to order on the tablet — it removes the counter bottleneck
pains.fix2: Customers enter their own order; name/price are snapshotted so later menu edits don't touch old orders
pains.fix3: Orders can only come from a device the shop activated — nobody can fire orders from outside
pains.pain4: No idea who the regulars are or what sells best
pains.fix4: Optional name+phone builds a per-shop customer history, plus best-seller and daily sales stats

demo.title: Short demo (2–3 minutes)
demo.subtitle: Show both the customer side and the shop side
demo.step1Detail: Lock the screen on the ordering view; after idle it shows ‘Tap to order’. Exit needs the shop's own PIN.
demo.step2Detail: Let the owner pick the menu into the cart themselves — they feel how easy it is.
demo.step3Detail: The QR is generated for the exact amount instantly, or choose cash — the shop confirms payment itself, no gateway fees.
demo.step4Detail: The order lands in the queue instantly, moving through accepted → preparing → ready → completed.
demo.step5Detail: Scan the QR on the kiosk screen and open /me on a phone to view that customer's own order history.

faq.title: Objections you'll hear + answers
faq.subtitle: Answer short, honest, and direct
faq.a1: Service is prepaid daily via PromptPay per the shop's plan — a light daily payment, no contract. Details are on /info.
faq.q2: Do I have to buy extra hardware?
faq.a2: No — it's a website that runs on a tablet/phone the shop already has. No app install.
faq.q3: What if the internet goes down?
faq.a3: Be honest: the system needs a network for live orders and the queue. If the connection drops temporarily, take orders the old way until it's back — then kiosk just resumes, no re-setup needed.
faq.q4: Some customers won't touch a tablet…
faq.a4: That's fine — staff can open orders at the counter for them (POS mode), and it's logged who opened the order.
faq.q5: How is this different from a regular POS?
faq.a5: It's self-order kiosk first, aiming to cut queues; no expensive hardware lock-in, just a tablet on the web, and it's a light daily payment.

close.title: Closing
close.subtitle: Soft close with a clear next step
close.script: "No decision needed right now — let me register your shop first, and the system will set up an account with your own menu. We'll run it together from there; if it doesn't work for you, we can talk anytime."
close.step1: If the shop is interested — push forward immediately; don't leave it as "I'll think about it and call you back".
close.step2: Register at least one lead before leaving (create at /admin/leads/new or view at /admin/leads)
close.step3: Log the visit with the sales status (interested / won) so follow-up is easy

sell.footerNote: This page is an internal playbook for the {brand} sales team — keep it open on site.
